name: Training Datasets
blurb: Corpora used to pre-train models, with provenance and licence.

items.note: Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus; trained T5 and remains the most-downloaded classic pretraining set
15 trillion tokens of filtered CommonCrawl; the reference open web-scale pretraining corpus
The education-filtered FineWeb subset that lifted small-model benchmarks and set the quality-over-quantity pattern
The largest fully open corpus built from public-domain and permissioned text only
6TB of permissively-licensed source code behind StarCoder; gated with an opt-out process for authors
The 825GB corpus that defined open pretraining data in the GPT-Neo era; historically important, now superseded
AI2's 3-trillion-token corpus with full documentation of what went in and why; trained the OLMo models
Open reproduction of the LLaMA training mix

reading.body:
C4's download count, at 1.3 million, is more than three times the next most-downloaded dataset here, making it the single most-used open pretraining corpus in this set despite being older and smaller than several alternatives.

The pattern across these eight datasets is a steady shift toward scale and curation. The Pile at 825 GB defined what open pretraining data looked like in an earlier era and now draws fewer than 5,000 downloads. FineWeb at 15 trillion tokens and Dolma at 3 trillion tokens reflect the current norm, where raw size is assumed and the distinguishing work is documentation of provenance and filtering decisions. FineWeb-Edu makes the quality-over-quantity logic explicit: a smaller, education-filtered subset lifted benchmark scores, and its download count of 391,000 is close to FineWeb's 419,000, suggesting practitioners treat them as comparable options rather than treating size as automatically decisive.

Licence and access conditions split the set cleanly. Five datasets carry an ODC-BY licence and are ungated. The Stack is gated and carries an opt-out process for authors, a different governance model reflecting the legal sensitivity of source code. Two datasets list no licence at all, which leaves their reuse terms unclear. What this data does not cover is the compute required to actually train on these corpora. Downloading a 15-trillion-token dataset and ingesting it into a training run are separated by a very large quantity of power, storage, and processing time, none of which appears here.
